reasoning: The lectures support several large aims: foundational XR concepts and issues; hardware, tracking, and software analysis; human-factors and perceptual design; user-centered requirements and system design; implementation with prototyping and engine/SDK work; empirical evaluation; and optimization of experience and resources. I grouped them by these aims while keeping the Majuli case study distributed across design, implementation, evaluation, and optimization. Lecture 63 is assigned to the foundational goal because it consolidates scope, boundaries, and further learning.

G1.goal: Explain XR, VR, AR, and MR through their definitions, application domains, system categories, historical evolution, and major psycho-physiological and technological issues.
G1.achieves: Lets the learner situate immersive technologies, recognize the presence, fidelity, tracking, and cybersickness challenges that shape XR design, and identify the boundaries of foundational XR system development.

G2.goal: Analyze the hardware, tracking, and software components of VR and AR systems, including input, processing, output, pose tracking, virtual world generation, and deployment tools.
G2.achieves: Lets the learner select and evaluate XR technologies and tools when planning or building an immersive system.

G3.goal: Apply user-centered, perceptual, and sensory foundations to design and assess immersive XR experiences involving vision, hearing, and other senses.
G3.achieves: Lets the learner make design and evaluation decisions that support presence and reduce sensory conflict, discomfort, or cybersickness.

G4.goal: Plan and design an XR system by applying the interactive-system development lifecycle, gathering usability requirements, and specifying interface, object-interaction, navigation, and system-control behavior.
G4.achieves: Lets the learner produce a coherent, user-centered XR system design with usability requirements, content strategy, and interaction plan for implementation.

G5.goal: Implement an XR system by choosing a lifecycle, creating and evaluating prototypes, and using Unity with rendering, physics, animation, audio, scripting, and an AR SDK to build and deploy an application.
G5.achieves: Lets the learner create a working XR or AR prototype and use practical engine and SDK skills to move a design into a deployable system.

G6.goal: Evaluate an XR system using self-report instruments, controlled empirical usability studies, and statistical analysis of presence, usability, and cybersickness.
G6.achieves: Lets the learner design and interpret evidence-based user evaluations to identify and justify improvements to an XR system.

G7.goal: Optimize XR experiences and resources by applying cybersickness-aware navigation and tour-planning methods and analyzing graphics-pipeline, rendering, and deployment requirements.
G7.achieves: Lets the learner reduce discomfort and computational cost while preserving presence and content fidelity in an XR system.
